idiom_name: C11 <stdatomic.h> atomic_compare_exchange_weak retry loop (Michael-Scott), or liburcu cds queues
implementation_notes: C11 supplies the primitive but not the structure: _Atomic endpoint words with atomic_compare_exchange_weak_explicit in a retry loop implement enqueue/dequeue exactly as Michael & Scott published, and nothing in the standard says when a dequeued node may be freed. Practical C therefore takes one of two paths: a bounded ring of slots with per-slot sequence numbers, which has no reclamation problem at all, or liburcu's Concurrent Data Structures, where rculfqueue.h is an RCU queue with lock-free enqueue and dequeue whose existence guarantees come from RCU, and wfcqueue.h provides a wait-free enqueue with blocking and non-blocking dequeue. Hand-rolling a linked queue is justified for teaching or when neither liburcu nor Concurrency Kit can be linked; in that case use a type-stable pool and never plain free().
pitfalls: Without a reclamation scheme the first removed node that a stalled thread still references is a use-after-free; ABA on recycled addresses needs a tag/counter or the same scheme.
A general-purpose malloc/free inside the operation is not lock-free - the allocator may lock; bounded arrays or pre-allocated pools keep the promise.
memory_order_relaxed on the publication or the claim breaks visibility; publish with release, observe with acquire, and stress-test with ThreadSanitizer.
